toc.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit; PR: pull request; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; CLI: command-line interface

  • What the exam is: 60 scenario-based items, 120 minutes, a scaled score of 720 to pass
  • The five domains, their weights and the 30 task statements behind them
  • The six scenarios (you meet four of them on exam day) and which domains each one tests
  • The ten decision rules that explain most correct answers
  • How the course is built and how to use it

Who this exam is for. A solution architect with about six months of hands-on work with the Claude API, the Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The exam tests judgment about trade-offs in production, not vocabulary.

2The Exam at a Glance

Fact Value (guide v1.0, July 2026)
Credential / code Claude Architect – Foundations / CCAR-F
Items 60, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select
Structure 4 scenarios picked at random from a bank of 6; the questions are framed by the scenario
Time 120 minutes (about 2 minutes per item)
Passing score 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000 (criterion-referenced: you are measured against a fixed standard, not against other candidates)
Fee USD 125 per attempt [Verify live]
Delivery Proctored by Pearson VUE: online or at a test center; closed book
Validity 12 months; renewal on time is a free, non-proctored assessment; a lapsed credential needs the full exam again
Retakes Wait 14 days after the first failed attempt, 30 after the second, 90 after the third; at most 4 attempts in a rolling 12 months; limits are per exam
Score report Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (the domain figures do not decide pass or fail)

Who can sit it [Verify live]. Exams are open to people who work at organizations in the Claude Partner Network, registering with a company email on the organization's listed domain; candidates must be 18 or older with a government photo ID whose name matches the registration. People outside the network can take the free Anthropic Academy courses, which give completion certificates, not the credential. This course teaches the same knowledge to everyone.

Exam tip

Item formats are not scored differently. For a multiple-response item the stem says how many to pick: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

3The Five Domains

Domain Weight Task statements Course modules
D1 Agentic Architecture and Orchestration 27% 1.1 to 1.7 (7) 1 to 4
D2 Tool Design and MCP Integration 18% 2.1 to 2.5 (5) 5 and 6
D3 Claude Code Configuration and Workflows 20% 3.1 to 3.6 (6) 7 and 8
D4 Prompt Engineering and Structured Output 20% 4.1 to 4.6 (6) 9 to 11
D5 Context Management and Reliability 15% 5.1 to 5.6 (6) 12 to 14
  • The weights are the approximate share of scored items: of 60 items, about 16 come from D1, 11 from D2, 12 from D3, 12 from D4 and 9 from D5.
  • Each task statement lists Knowledge of (concepts) and Skills in (what you can do); items are written against them.
  • Out of scope (will not appear): fine-tuning or training models; API authentication, billing or account management; programming-language specifics; deploying or hosting MCP servers; model internals, RLHF or Constitutional AI; embeddings and vector databases; computer use; vision; streaming and server-sent events; rate limits, quotas or pricing math; OAuth and key rotation; cloud-provider setup; benchmarking; prompt caching details; tokenization.

4The Six Scenarios

Running case

Birchwood Supply

  • Throughout the course you follow Birchwood Supply, a fictional online retailer
  • Its support agent answers returns and billing questions, its research assistant writes market reports, and its engineers use Claude Code every day
  • Each module solves one problem of this company; the questions use the same style as the exam scenarios

# Scenario What you build Primary domains
1 Customer Support Resolution Agent Agent SDK agent with MCP tools get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human; target 80%+ first-contact resolution and knowing when to escalate D1, D2, D5
2 Code Generation with Claude Code Team use of Claude Code: slash commands, CLAUDE.md, plan mode vs direct execution D3, D5
3 Multi-Agent Research System Coordinator with subagents: web search, document analysis, synthesis, report generation; cited reports D1, D2, D5
4 Developer Productivity with Claude Agent SDK tools to explore codebases, using Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob and MCP servers D2, D3, D1
5 Claude Code for Continuous Integration Automated code review, test generation and PR feedback in CI; minimize false positives D3, D4
6 Structured Data Extraction Extract data from unstructured documents, validate with JSON schemas, handle edge cases D4, D5
Exam tip

You will not know in advance which four scenarios you get, so study all six. Module 15 walks through each one from the first requirement to the best architecture.

5Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

Most items present a problem seen in logs or production data and four plausible fixes. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Learn them now; each later module shows them at work.

# Rule Typical wrong answers
1 A hard business requirement needs programmatic enforcement (hooks, prerequisite gates), because prompts have a non-zero failure rate Stronger system prompt wording, more few-shot examples
2 Find the root cause from the evidence given before choosing the fix (the logs usually name it) Blaming a downstream agent that behaved correctly
3 Choose the proportionate first step: low effort, high leverage (better tool descriptions, explicit criteria, a few examples) before new infrastructure A separate classifier, a routing layer, fine-tuning
4 Least privilege: each agent gets only the tools its role needs, plus a narrow shared tool for a frequent need Giving every agent every tool
5 Structured beats generic: structured errors, structured handoffs, claim-to-source mappings, case-fact blocks "Operation failed", free-text summaries
6 Self-reported confidence and sentiment are weak proxies for difficulty; use explicit criteria and calibrated, validated signals "Escalate when confidence < 7", sentiment thresholds
7 Independent review beats self-review; split big reviews into per-file passes plus an integration pass Asking the same session to double-check itself; a bigger context window
8 Match the API to the latency need: synchronous for blocking steps, batch for overnight work Batch for pre-merge checks
9 Never suppress errors and never abort everything: return partial results with failure context and annotate gaps Empty result marked as success; kill the whole run on one timeout
10 Context is a budget: isolate verbose work in subagents, persist key facts outside summaries, trim tool output Reading everything up front, relying on a long history
Exam tip

When two options both "work", prefer the one that is deterministic, specific, scoped and proportionate. Words like "always", "guarantee" and "must" in the requirement point to rule 1.

6The Technologies at a Glance

Piece What it is Exam focus
Claude API The Messages API: send messages, define tools (tool_use), steer with tool_choice, read stop_reason, cap output with max_tokens, set a system prompt; Message Batches API for asynchronous bulk work D1 loops, D2 tool_choice, D4 structured output and batches
Claude Agent SDK The same agent loop that powers Claude Code, as a library: tools, subagents, hooks, sessions D1, D2, D5
Claude Code The coding agent and CLI: CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, plan mode, MCP servers, -p for scripts and CI D3, D2
MCP (Model Context Protocol) An open standard to connect tools (actions), resources (read-only content catalogs) and prompts to an agent D2
JSON Schema / Pydantic Describe and validate structured output D4

7How to Use This Course

  • Order: read modules 1 to 14 in order (they follow the guide's domains), then module 15 (scenarios), 16 (recap) and 17 (exam technique).
  • Each module has task statements, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, six or more scenario questions with explanations, and a Quick Reference Card.
  • Hands-on practice matters. The guide recommends four exercises: (1) a multi-tool agent with escalation logic; (2) Claude Code configured for a team (CLAUDE.md, rules, a skill, an MCP server); (3) a structured extraction pipeline with validation, retry and batches; (4) a multi-agent research pipeline with error propagation and provenance. Do at least the first two with real code.
  • Product details change fast (tool names, flags, model behavior). Boxes marked [Verify live] show where the current documentation differs from the wording of the guide; on the exam, answer as the guide teaches.
  • Independence. This course is independent study material; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic or Pearson VUE. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

8Exam Q&A

S1On exam day a candidate meets a multiple-response item whose stem says to choose two answers. Which approach is correct?

  • ASelect one option and leave the second blank to avoid a penalty
  • BSelect exactly two options, the two that best satisfy the requirement
  • CSelect three options so at least two are correct
  • DSelect all options that look plausible, because partial answers get partial credit
Show the answer

Answer: B. The stem states how many responses to select; choose exactly that many. Selecting more or fewer does not follow the item's instruction.

S2A candidate scored 700 overall but 90% in one domain. What is the result?

  • AFail, because the total scaled score of 700 is below 720
  • BFail, because each of the five domains must individually reach a scaled score of 720
  • CPass, because one domain is above 80%
  • DPass, because domain scores average out
Show the answer

Answer: A. The result is based on the total scaled score (cut score 720). Domain percentages are shown on the report for guidance only.

S3Which topic is out of scope for the exam?

  • AChoosing between the synchronous API and the Message Batches API
  • BDesigning structured error responses for an MCP tool
  • CFine-tuning a Claude model on company data
  • DWriting a path-scoped rule file for Claude Code
Show the answer

Answer: C. Fine-tuning and training custom models are listed as out of scope; the other three are in the blueprint.

S4Which domain carries the largest share of the scored items?

  • APrompt Engineering and Structured Output
  • BContext Management and Reliability
  • CAgentic Architecture and Orchestration
  • DTool Design and MCP Integration
Show the answer

Answer: C. Domain 1, Agentic Architecture and Orchestration, is 27%, the largest. Study it first and most.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam CCAR-F; 60 items; 120 min; 4 of 6 scenarios; pass 720 of 1,000; USD 125; valid 12 months
Domains D1 27 Agentic · D2 18 Tools and MCP · D3 20 Claude Code · D4 20 Prompts and structured output · D5 15 Context and reliability
Task statements 30 in all: 7, 5, 6, 6, 6
Scenarios Support agent · Claude Code codegen · Multi-agent research · Developer productivity · Claude Code in CI · Structured extraction
Retakes 14, 30, 90 days; max 4 per rolling 12 months
Eligibility Partner Network staff with a company email [Verify live]; Academy courses give completion certificates only
Ten rules Enforce in code · find the root cause · proportionate first step · least privilege · structured beats generic · distrust self-reported confidence · independent review · match API to latency · no silent errors, no total aborts · context is a budget
